title: Secure Delegation PRD: SSO/SAML + RBAC + KMS/HSM gap analysis and phased integration matrix
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Purpose: capture a product requirements doc (PRD) and an integration/gating matrix for a secure delegation model covering SSO (SAML), RBAC roles for operator vs. customer scopes, and KMS/HSM interactions for customer key custody. This ticket scopes the gap analysis between current Redwood Private capabilities and enterprise needs, defines measurable acceptance criteria, and produces a phased checklist that engineering, security, and solutions can sign off on. The output will include: 1) a short PRD with user flows for operator-managed vs customer-managed keys; 2) a matrix mapping features to release phase (alpha: limited customers; beta: partner programs; GA: broad availability); 3) test/verification criteria for SAML metadata refresh, assertion replay protection, RBAC least-privilege roles, audit log immutability, and HSM escrow/rotation drills.
acceptance_criteria: SAML: metadata refresh cycle <= 24 hours; automated CI job to validate incoming IdP certs and raise alerts on mismatch
SSO assertions: replay protection and nonce validation verified by integration test harness; failed replay attempts generate high-priority audit entries
RBAC: predefined role templates (CustomerAdmin, CustomerOperator, RedwoodOperator) implemented and documented; least-privilege baseline validated by policy linting tool
KMS/HSM: customer-key unwrap API flows succeed end-to-end with hardware-backed keys in lab (HSM model Y) and fallback to software-wrapped keys in airgapped mode
Audit logs: append-only storage with hash-chained integrity check; 90-day retention by default and configurable up to 7 years with export path to customer bucket
Operator delegation: clear boundaries documented and tested so that operator actions require explicit delegated grants; automated alerts on privilege escalation attempts
Operational runbook: key rotation, compromise drill, and post-incident evidence collection documented and exercise-tested with SRE team
Performance: key unwrap path latency P95 <= 120ms in dedicated capacity test harness for 8kB payloads
Telemetry: rollout exposes per-tenant metrics (successful/failed auth, key operations, RBAC changes) to Console within 60s of event ingestion

SRE: operational runbook validated in tabletop exercise (date + notes in comments)
Solutions/SE: customer acceptance test (CAT) template created and validated with two pilot accounts
Legal/Compliance: data residency and export control signoff for customer key export flows

Documentation: Console UX flows, API reference, and RBAC role doc published to docs.redwood.ai
decisions: Chosen HSM integration model: HSM proxy adapter with customer-controlled key material; avoids embedding vendor SDKs in the control plane
RBAC model: hybrid approach (templated roles + fine-grained grants) to reduce friction for initial customers
SAML approach: support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows; require signed assertions for all customer tenants
Audit storage: use tamper-evident append-only store backed by object immutability + periodic Merkle snapshotting
tradeoffs: HSM proxy increases operational complexity (engineers + runbooks) but preserves customer key custody guarantees compared to full-embedded HSM drivers
Tighter SAML assertion validation increases rejection rates for misconfigured IdPs; to mitigate we provide a validation sandbox and better error messaging
Longer retention for logs increases cost; we propose tiered retention with archive/export options to offload cold data to customer buckets
